text:
The most beautiful bibingka pancake ever with a salted egg filling…from a local gem serving Filipino-inspired brunch in Jersey City 🌺🇵🇭

@next_door_provisions is a cozy, mom-and-pop restaurant run by a husband-and-wife duo, where Chef Ruby Felix-Curtis is the mastermind behind all the creative fusion dishes. I honestly want to try EVERY SINGLE ITEM on the menu😭

✎﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏

🍔 𝙇𝙤𝙣𝙜𝙖𝙣𝙞𝙯𝙯𝙖 𝙎𝙡𝙞𝙙𝙚𝙧𝙨 $16
Weekend special. As a longanizza lover, this might be the best slider I’ve had in a long time. Super juicy pork patty with bang bang sauce. Heard there’s a chance it’ll stay on the regular menu if enough people show it some love👀

🍝 𝙆𝙖𝙧𝙚 𝙆𝙖𝙧𝙚 𝙈𝙖𝙛𝙖𝙡𝙙𝙞𝙣𝙞 $28 
Inspired by Filipino kare kare, they toss fresh handmade malfadini in a rich peanut sauce with shrimp paste instead of serving it over rice. The sauce takes 6 hours to make, and the beef brisket is braised for 3 hours. Truly a labor of love! Even the Peruvian pepper was so juicy I wanted more🤤

🥞 𝘽𝙞𝙗𝙞𝙣𝙜𝙠𝙖 𝙋𝙖𝙣𝙘𝙖𝙠𝙚 $17
Every table ordered the bibingka pancake. Our jaws literally dropped when it arrived. MASSIVE, super fluffy, moist, and packed with salted egg (both the yolk and the white!). Though we did find it a little too salty after a few bites. We had leftovers for two more meals🤯

✎﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏

📍 𝗡𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗗𝗼𝗼𝗿 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

text:
✨ BOUJEE SUSIE’S TOP 5 NEW YORK RESTAURANTS

1. THE GRILL 🥩
Old-school Manhattan glamour. Huge dining room, iconic interiors and serious New York power-lunch energy.

2. LE COUCOU 🕯️
Romantic, candlelit and effortlessly chic. Gorgeous French food and one of the prettiest dining rooms downtown.

3. COTE 🔥
Korean steakhouse meets New York nightlife. Dark, sexy, lively and perfect for a proper night out.

4. MANHATTA 🗽
Come for the food… but WOW, those views. Floor-to-ceiling Manhattan skyline from 60 floors up. Book around sunset.

5. THE RIVER CAFÉ 🌉
Possibly the most romantic setting of them all. Right beneath Brooklyn Bridge with incredible views back across Manhattan.

✨ Boujee Susie Verdict: Five completely different restaurants, five fabulous New York experiences. And yes… these are all worth dressing up for. 😂🥂

text:
New Cocktail & Vinyl Listening Lounge In New York City 🎶🍸💿

If you’re looking for new bars in Brooklyn or a unique NYC date night spot, add Don’t Matter in DUMBO to your list.

📍 55 Sands Street, DUMBO, Brooklyn
🗓️ Wednesday–Sunday
💡 Perfect for: date night, drinks with friends + music lovers

🎶 THE VIBE: Inspired by Japanese listening bars, the space is designed around a curated vinyl collection and custom sound system, with DJs spinning everything from R&B and soul to reggae, hip-hop, rock and more.

🍸 DRINKS: The cocktail menu features some really creative flavor combinations using ingredients like passionfruit, shiso, yuzu, ginger and Thai basil. They also have wine, beer and non-alcoholic options.

🍽️ BITES: Pair your drinks with Pan-Caribbean-inspired small plates made for sharing, including tuna tartlets, shrimp cocktail, crispy mushroom sliders, plantain chips and more.

🌃 THE SPACE: There’s an intimate indoor listening lounge plus an outdoor deck, making it such a cool spot to grab drinks, listen to great music and spend the evening with friends.

Definitely one to put on your radar if you’re looking for new things to do in Brooklyn, cool bars in DUMBO or unique NYC nightlife experiences. 💿✨

1. The Ripple Room in Nolita, is a 70’s style bar with two pool tables. Great for a pint, cocktail and a game of pool catching up.

text:
Moru in Fort Lee, New Jersey, is a modern Japanese fusion restaurant centered around sushi, sashimi, and hand rolls with Korean influences. The katsu sando was easily one of the best I’ve had—the pork is lightly seasoned so its natural flavor comes through, while the sauce brings out a deeper sweetness and umami. Their summer set with soba, salmon sashimi, and tonkatsu was also excellent. Mixing a little wasabi into the soba broth adds a sharp, aromatic kick, bringing out its savory depth along with the subtle sweetness and saltiness that coat the noodles beautifully. I especially liked the balance between the light, refreshing soba and the richer tonkatsu. Even the lettuce salad works well—the dressing leans sweet, but it has a brighter, fresher sweetness than the tonkatsu sauce, helping reset the palate between bites. If you ever find yourself passing through Fort Lee, Moru is definitely worth a stop.

text:
Zoli is a new American restaurant opening soon at the Amant arts campus in East Williamsburg, Brooklyn. Led by chef Ned Baldwin (of Houseman), it offers thoughtful, ingredient-driven cooking in a stylish space designed by GRT Architects. It opens on April 29th.

Inside, the standout artwork is Pierre Huyghe’s site-specific aquarium titled “Satellite”.  A striking three-tank triptych that divides the bar from the main dining room. It is directly inspired by New York’s local waters, specifically the polluted industrial waterway of Newtown Creek (a Superfund site next to Amant). The piece incorporates reconstructed debris from Brooklyn’s creeks, horseshoe crabs, a “toxic” looking seabed aesthetic, and living elements to explore themes of pollution, evolution, nature, and human impact.

Smart glass panels can turn opaque or transparent, creating shifting, rhythmic scenes visible from the dining room and even the street. The restaurant blends seamlessly with Amant’s mission, turning the dining experience into a creative and social hub.

The menu is fish-forward, drawing inspiration from chef Baldwin’s background as a Long Island fisherman. It features progressive American cooking with high-quality, seasonal ingredients and a plethora of aged and preserved items. Expect dishes that pair beautifully with the artistic setting, alongside house-brewed kombucha, cocktails, and wine.

Are you going?

Looking for where to eat in Midtown Manhattan? 🗽

Save these five restaurants for your next New York City trip — all around Midtown, but each offering a completely different dining experience.

🥃 The Polo Bar for a timeless New York dinner, classic atmosphere and one of Manhattan’s most iconic dining rooms.

🍸 Monkey Bar for that unmistakable old-school NYC feeling, great cocktails and a lively dinner in the heart of Midtown.

🥢 53 for contemporary Asian cuisine, beautiful design and a sophisticated night out near MoMA and Fifth Avenue.

🍣 Nobu Fifty Seven for sushi, Japanese cuisine and the Nobu classics — an easy choice for lunch or dinner while exploring Midtown Manhattan.

🍝 Casa Lever for elegant Italian cuisine on Park Avenue, perfect for a business lunch, date night or a more polished dinner in New York.

Whether you’re staying near Fifth Avenue, Central Park, Rockefeller Center, Park Avenue or Midtown East, these are five Manhattan restaurants worth adding to your list.

Five different cuisines, five different atmospheres and five very good reasons to make a reservation.

New York has endless restaurants. These are a few we’d happily go back to.

text:
🌿 Stop scrolling… this might be the best day date in New Jersey. ❤️

I finally checked out Grounds for Sculpture in Hamilton, NJ, and now I understand why so many people recommend it. If you’re looking for a unique New Jersey date idea, this is one to add to your list.

Spend the day wandering through beautiful gardens, discovering incredible sculptures around every corner, and taking in all the little hidden spots that make this place so special. It feels like you’re stepping into a work of art.

When you need a break, you don’t even have to leave the grounds. Grab a latte from the Van Gogh Café, enjoy a meal at the iconic Rat’s Restaurant, or stop by the brand-new Peacock Cantina for Mexican-inspired food and drinks. 🌮☕

I’m sharing more about Peacock Cantina in my next video because it deserves its own spotlight, so stay tuned!

📍Grounds for Sculpture

text:
@TheLola officially launched a brand-new dinner experience, andI am BLOWN away. From the moment you walk in, you’re met with an elegant, moody cocktail lounge paired with elevated dining energy—chic, warm, and inviting. It’s giving NYC without going to the city 🍸

The LOLA partnered with Chef Brandon “Bud” Carter (current chef at Olea in Spring Lake and former chef at Butcher’s Block) to design a steak, pasta, and seafood-forward menu—and it absolutely delivered. Every dish felt intentional, balanced, and beautifully executed.

What we ordered:
🍸 Dirty Little Secret- dirty martini (extra olive juice, served as two pours)
🍸 Espresso martini
🍸 Bella Ciao 
🍸 French Lace
🥢 Crab rangoon
🐟 Tuna tostada
🍝 Spicy rigatoni
🥩 Ribeye
🍗 Roasted Half Chicken 
🥔 Crispy potatoes

Dessert:
🍩 Churro Crullers 
🍰 Blueberry cheesecake bread pudding 
🍰 Biscoff cheesecake

The cocktail program is elevated with the martini at its core—and it’s absolutely one I’ll be returning for. The bar itself is a vibe on its own: great cocktails, great energy, and perfect for walk-ins.

Good to know:
✨ Elegant dining experience
🕙 Last dinner seating at 10:30 PM
🕑 All rooms open until 2 AM
📅 Reservations release one month in advance—book quickly

text:
I visited Melba’s in Harlem to try soul food for the 1st time 🖤✊🏾

Soul food is the ethnic cuisine of African Americans, with a very deep and rich historical significance. Soul food refers to the recipes rooted in the cooking techniques and traditions developed by enslaved people in the southern United States, who used ingenuity to create nutritious meals out of the very little that was made available to them, in order to survive. Soul food is now a celebration of comfort, resilience, togetherness and an important part of Black American heritage.

text:
❗️INSANE UNDERGROUND RESTAURANT IN NYC: DO NOT DISTURB 🔥 This hidden gem is tucked underneath the streets of Manhattan’s West Village and waiting inside is a crazy menu of food + all types of vibes. Do Not Disturb has become one of my favorite city joints and it’s not hard to see why. 

📌 In terms of food, you can dig into both humble grub as well as curated high end plates. All are chef crafted and crush it on unique but wildly delicious flavor. The crispy rice selection is top tier, the Smashburger is easily one of Manhattans best & their lemon pepper wings BANG. But if you want something a bit more fancy, the lobster pasta is a sure shot and the lamb is *chefs kiss* 

👉 But what makes this place even more of a standout is the various vibes you’ll find throughout there multiple rooms. You can easily have a beautiful date night here or hit it for a friend’s night out and honestly it will deliver equally on both moods. 

🫡 Throw this West Village hidden gem at the top of your NYC grub list & thank me later. 

📍 West Village, Manhattan, NYC

you can have dinner inside this 100-year-old bank in Westwood, NJ 🍴

@the_rosangellys in Westwood just started serving dinner so of course we had to go check it out. The Latin-inspired menu is influenced by owners Sebastian Perez and Rosangelly Flores’ Colombian and Puerto Rican roots. We loved trying dishes like the Braised Short Ribs, Peruvian Pollo a la Brasa, and Mango Tres Leches Cake. And JSYK, it’s BYOB.

The restaurant is actually located inside the Westwood Trust Building, a former bank and local historic landmark. And don’t worry, they kept the original floors and wood paneling to preserve it and added some tasteful modern updates that we looove.

📍 1 Westwood Avenue, Westwood

A new Japanese restaurant has officially opened in Bergen County 🍜🍤

Gomen is now open in downtown Ridgewood, describing itself as a “Japanese Kitchen Lab” focused on Japanese comfort food

The menu includes kaisen, tempura, katsu, ramen and udon, with the kitchen led by a chef with more than 15 years of experience with traditional tendon and ramen

The name combines “gohan,” meaning rice, and “men,” meaning noodle— while “gomen” also translates to “I’m sorry” in Japanese

text:
Champagne cart brunch? Say less 🥂

New York City brunch just leveled up. One of my favorites, Café Carmellini (inside The Fifth Avenue Hotel) is now serving a weekend brunch that feels equal parts elegant and indulgent.

There’s a two-course menu ($65pp) featuring chef Andrew Carmellini’s signature dishes, plus a rolling Champagne cart loaded with beautiful bottles (showstopper energy).

To start: fresh seasonal fruit and a gorgeous spread of housemade pastries with cultured butter and preserves. Then choose from a dozen tempting entrées — think crêpe Suzette flambéed French toast, smoked salmon Benedict, lobster frittata, rabbit pappardelle, and flat iron tagliata & eggs.

And yes, the caviar service is optional (but is it really?) — a generous helping of Osetra served with all the accompaniments and the most dreamy, warm potato blinis. Worth it. 

Live music from the mezzanine adds to the ambiance, making it easily one of the best upscale brunches in the city — set in one of the most stunning dining rooms.

Save this for your next brunch date and tag who you’re bringing 🥂

#nycbrunch #cafecarmellini #champagne #brunch #nycrestaurants 

@The Fifth Avenue Hotel

text:
The River Palm Terrace in Edgewater, New Jersey AKA sushi and a steak! How can you go wrong with either of those?! 🍣🥩 🤤

Come along with me to one of my favorite restaurants, The River Palm Terrace in Edgewater, NJ! 🤍 If you know me, you know this is one of my go-to spots whenever I’m craving amazing sushi and steak.

We started with drinks before ordering our favorite appetizer—Ōtoro crispy rice. Ōtoro is the premium, buttery cut of tuna belly that literally melts in your mouth, and paired with crispy rice, it’s absolutely incredible. We also shared a few sushi rolls before our entrées.

I ordered the New York strip with truffle fries and creamy spinach, while my husband went with the chicken Parmesan. Every single dish was delicious!

This is one of those restaurants that never misses, and it’s the reason we keep coming back. If you’re in the Edgewater area, The River Palm Terrace is definitely worth a visit!

text:
Some restaurants are worth dressing up for and Rampoldi is one of them 😏❤️

Rampoldi brings the glamour of Monte-Carlo to the Upper West Side with a menu that beautifully blends French and Italian flavors.

📍Rampoldi NYC / 49 W 64th St, New York City

We ordered:
🍸Caesar Salad
🍸Duck Confit w/ a rich red wine and berry sauce + potatoes
🍸Red Wine Braised Beef 
🍸Lobster Pasta 
🍸Lemon Meringue

Every plate looked as luxurious as it tasted. If I had to recommend two items to make the perfect dinner it would for sure be the Duck Confit and the Braised Beef. My go to drink is always a Side Car (with a sugar rim) and one sip of theirs had me feeling good! I’d come back for that just alone. 

If you're planning your next date night, celebrating something special, or simply want an excuse to treat yourself, add this one to your NYC list.

text:
Buddy's - their pancakes are incredible and have such fun flavors. You really can't go wrong with anything you get on the menu here

Lokal - brunch with an incredible view here. They bring out fresh pastries when you sit down which I love. I have never left disappointed. Also the short ribs hash and eggs is my favorite 

Madame - the ultimate girls night out dinner spot. Drinks incredible. Food incredible. In a kinda tucked away spot but well worth it. 

Razza - there's a reason they are famous for their pizza. It was so good we finished one pie and ordered another. And please do yourself a favor and order the olive oil cake. 

Domodomo - really the only "upscale" sushi place in JC and perfect for a date night. Also ordering it in is fun because it comes in a fancy box and tastes just a fresh as in person. 

Downtown froyo - I am a regular here. Not joking I get it every week and it is the highlight of my week. Love this place so much and you get to customize your froyo which is so fun.

text:
🥞 This Jersey hotspot takes indulgence to the next level with sky-high pancakes, insane milkshakes, and a menu so big you’ll have trouble choosing.

🍔 The burgers here are anything but ordinary. Take the Man vs. Burger—a towering masterpiece sandwiched between two grilled cheese sandwiches instead of a bun. It’s a melty, cheesy, flavor-packed challenge that’s as fun to eat as it is delicious.

🍦 And then there are the crazy milkshakes. These aren’t just drinks—they’re fully loaded desserts stacked with donuts, cookies, brownies, and even entire slices of cake. Sweet tooth? Consider it handled.

🎡 Whether you’re here for a classic stack of pancakes or a burger that defies logic, this spot makes sure every meal is an unforgettable experience. Chen out the  Brownstone Pancake Factory in NJ!

text:
Basement is a subterranean techno club in Queens, NYC, tucked beneath the Knockdown Center in what used to be an industrial factory space. You walk in through a long, narrow concrete tunnel that already feels like part of the experience, gradually pulling you away from the street and into a darker, enclosed world.​

Inside, the ceilings are low, with exposed brick, raw concrete pillars and very minimal lighting that keeps most of the room in shadow while still making the crowd and pathways feel navigable. The layout is compact and focused around a powerful, carefully tuned sound system, so the music feels physical and immediate rather than just loud.​

Most of the original factory character is intentionally left visible: heavy doors, industrial textures, little or no decorative branding, and only the functional signage you actually need to move through the space. The overall feeling is more like an underground bunker or rehearsal space than a polished commercial nightclub, which fits the music and the crowd.​

The club runs with a strict no-photo approach and no bottle service, which means people are not holding up phones or clustered around tables; instead, almost everyone faces the booth and locks into the long, driving techno sets. This creates a concentrated atmosphere where the focus is sound, darkness and collective energy rather than social media moments or visual spectacle.

text:
New York City’s rooftop bars are more than just glamorous hangouts — they’re a living part of the city’s cultural evolution, blending architecture, nightlife, and skyline romance into one unforgettable experience.

The roots of rooftop socializing in New York trace back to the early 1900s, during the Golden Age of Broadway. As summer heat made enclosed theaters unbearable, hotel owners began opening rooftop gardens and open-air cafés atop grand hotels. Venues like the Astor Roof Garden (opened in 1904) and the Hotel Knickerbocker’s rooftop ballroom became fashionable escapes where the city’s elite could dine under the stars while listening to live orchestras. These spaces set the foundation for what would later become today’s modern rooftop bar culture — luxury and leisure elevated, quite literally, above the city bustle.

After a mid-century lull, rooftop nightlife re-emerged in the 1980s and 1990s, as Manhattan’s skyline became an icon of urban sophistication. Trendy venues like the Rainbow Room at Rockefeller Center revived the allure of panoramic views paired with cocktails, while the rise of boutique hotels brought an entirely new wave of elevated experiences.

text:
New York City is filled with world-famous restaurants, but some of the best meals are found in places that many visitors overlook. From cozy Italian trattorias and hidden alleyway eateries to neighborhood pizza shops and incredible Thai cuisine, these hidden gems prove you don't have to eat in Times Square to experience the city's best food. Whether you're craving handmade pasta, authentic New York-style pizza, creative international flavors, or classic American comfort food, these local favorites offer unforgettable meals and a unique dining experience. Many of these spots are loved by New Yorkers and food critics alike, yet they still feel like secrets compared to the city's biggest tourist destinations. If you're planning a trip to NYC or you're a local looking for your next favorite restaurant, be sure to save this list for later. Great food is waiting around every corner, you just have to know where to look. Follow for more hidden restaurants, travel guides, and bucket-list destinations across the United States!

text:
Forget the hyped spots, these late-night joints are where you really want to eat. Real food, no frills, and open late. Hit these places when the tourists are asleep:

• El Castillo de Jagua – Dominican diner, no BS, just good chicken.
• Pata Paplean – Thai street food in a dive bar, perfect for night owls.
• Ba Xuyên – Some of the best banh mi in the city, and cheap.
• Fat Buddha – Asian fusion, booze, and killer wings.
• Casa Adela – Puerto Rican rotisserie that’ll hit the spot.
• El Atoradero – Mexican food that’s actually legit.
• Benemon – Quiet Japanese comfort food, because ramen’s better at night.

Eat, don’t post.

FiDi officially has a new happy hour spot worth knowing about ☁️

If you're looking for a spot that feels elevated without the rooftop crowds, add Cloud One Wine Bar & Lounge to your list. Technically not a “Rooftop” but it’s located on the 6th floor inside of The Cloud One Hotel, overlooking the Freedom Tower with floor to ceiling windows and an outdoor terrace that's perfect for golden hour. 

📍The Cloud One Wine Bar & Lounge / 133 Greenwich St, New York City 

The wine program was curated by award-winning sommelier Mark Guillaudeu (of Eleven Madison Park), featuring sustainably produced wines from New York, California, and Oregon. They also have great speciality cocktails! You can pair your drinks with shareable bites like charcuterie, grilled cheese + locally inspired snacks, then settle in for one of the best sunset views in FiDi. #nyc #rooftop #happyhour #nychotel #nycdinner

👑 King Cole Bar — legendary at The St. Regis, home of the original Bloody Mary under the Old King Cole mural.
🌃 The Skylark — sleek rooftop with Empire State views and a chic all-seasons lounge.

text:
There’s something about a dimly lit bar, the hum of conversation, and a good drink in hand that makes winter in NYC feel downright romantic. And when there’s a fireplace involved? Even better.

If you’re looking for a cozy spot to warm up in Greenpoint, here are three bars that do ambiance right:

🔥 Achilles Heel – A neighborhood classic with an old-world feel. Think flickering candlelight, exposed brick, and a wood-burning fireplace that makes you want to settle in with a glass of something rich and bold. It’s effortlessly cool without trying too hard.

🍸 Little Rascal – The kind of place where you walk in for one drink and end up staying for hours. The cocktails are well-balanced, the crowd is always interesting, and there’s a warmth here—both in the lighting and the energy—that makes it feel like a secret you’re in on.

🥃 Glasserie – Tucked away with an intimate, almost otherworldly charm. Middle Eastern flavors meet moody interiors, making it the perfect spot for a long, lingering night with someone whose presence feels just as intoxicating as the drinks.

Where are your favorite cozy bars in NYC? Drop them in the comments—I’m always looking for my next go-to.

text:
cooks burger bar | williamsburg, va

shock and awe. thats what I feel for this place. this is one of the most perfectly executed restaurant spaces I have ever seen in my life. on top of that, its also one of the most perfectly satisfying burgers I have ever had.

the hunt for the best burger in the 757 brought us across the hrbt to midtown williamsburg this past weekend and it was worth every second of the drive! walk in and youre immediately transported to the 80s with the wood veneer walls, neon signs, and vintage mirrors obviously rescued from old dive bars or someone's basement. think stranger things, but without the monsters. arcade games up front and a disco ball really completed the vibes.

for sides, we got potato salad and farmers fries. the potato salad might be some of the best I've had in the area and I love the brightness of the dill in it! the farmers fries? send me to heaven now. I am so picky about homemade fries because they're often soggy or just poorly done. NOT HERE. they were so crispy and loaded down with pecorino with a side of roasted garlic aioli 🤌🏻

the burgers themselves were so nostalgic and perfect. cooked in tallow, the patties are reminiscent of your favorite fast food burger. they only give you two options on the cook: pink or no pink. my partner got the pastrami burger, which they smoke in house! definitely need to go back and try their reuben 👀 the burger also came with swiss, house made caraway kraut and house made 1000 island. what a flavor punch! omg it was messy and delicious, but the toast on the flaxseed brioche bun really held up to the sauciness!

I got a bacon cheese burger but added an onion ring. dude. I think i happy danced through this entire meal. everything was perfect. the bun, crispy on the cut side, soft inside, lovely little toasty flax seeds. the bacon? thick cut. the onion ring? a sweet, crispy monster of a thing.

I'm already craving another one.

text:
Panino Rustico is a Brooklyn South treasure. 🙏 I was born and raised in Bay Ridge, so today I stopped by Panino Rustico’s Bay Ridge location to kick off my Best of Brooklyn South series, and I ordered my all-time faves. Here’s how to order like me: 

Appetizer: 

-B6: Eggplant caponata with goat cheese

Main:

-P38: Grilled chicken, fontina, bacon, cherry pepper, avocado, honey mustard (+EXTRA honey mustard on the side)

Drinks: 

-Lemonade 
-Iced coffee (black + 2 pumps of hazelnut) 
-Water

Dessert: 

-Peanut butter & jelly crepe 
-Espresso 

Panino Rustico in Bay Ridge is spacious, with indoor and outdoor seating, and a full menu of sandwiches and crepes, offering a little bit of something for everyone. 🤤 Stop in at 8901 3rd Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11209. They’re open 7 days a week, on Monday - Saturday from 9 am - 8:30 pm, and Sunday from 9 am - 7:30 pm.

text:
I would fly back to New York just for this

I already love Chinese food, but this spot made me love it even more. We ordered so much off the menu, and honestly… I’d get almost everything again. Next time, I’d probably reorder all of these and just add new dishes on top.

I wish I had more footage because this meal deserved a longer video, but here’s everything I need to say about my favorites:

📍 Antidote in Brooklyn (I think they also have a second location)

Scallion pancake $12: So flaky and perfectly crisp

Dan dan noodles $14: Chewy noodles with the perfect balance of spice and sesame

Preserved egg with tofu $15: I was hesitant at first, but this ended up being one of my favorites. The flavor and spice were so good.

Sliced pork with garlic sauce $17: I can’t believe I didn’t include this in the video… this was actually my favorite dish 

Sichuan cold noodles $12: Super flavorful with that rich peanut sauce

I miss this place so much. I wasn’t planning a trip back to New York anytime soon… but honestly, I would go back just for Antidote.

#nyceats #chinesefood #brooklyneats #nycfood

text:
We ended up at Milk & Roses on a cold night in Greenpoint, the kind of cold that makes you want warmth that lasts longer than the walk inside.

The room held us gently. Low light, warm wood, candle glow softening everything it touched. We ordered Negronis and let the night slow to our pace.

Dinner followed. Pasticcio al Forno and Genovese al ragù di agnello. Both rich, both comforting. The kind of food that settles in, that invites you to stay present.

We sat side by side, hands intertwined, conversation moving easily, drifting and returning. Outside, the backyard garden glowed quietly. Somewhere nearby, a fireplace burned, steady and unhurried.

It was a night to be remembered.
Remembered, and felt.

#nyceats #romanticdinner #travel #nyctravel #traveljournal 

@milkandrosesbistro

text:
Soho makes dining feel spontaneous, but always on point. The best restaurants in Soho aren’t hard to find because they’re part of the neighbourhood’s rhythm. Tables tucked just off the pavement, lights low, conversation easy. You wander, something pulls you in, and somehow it’s always a good call. 
It’s not about trends or noise but it’s about places that get the details right: setting, service, timing, energy. There’s a reason people keep crossing town for dinner here. It delivers, quietly and consistently.

text:
Here are three different KBBQ restaurants I tried in New York City in 2024.

Coming in at #3 is Antoya, the food was a solid 8, but the crowd made it difficult to do anything but eat. Services was fast, I’d definitely come back here if I was in a pinch in K-Town.

#2 is Dons Bogam, we had so many dishes and a meat platter that was truly phenomenal. Food was a solid 8 as well, but what I liked here more than Antoya was how spread out the tables were. Service was also phenomenal here.

Coming in at #1, the place I literally dream about, Nubiani! This is owned by the same place at COTE. It’s so hard to get in to COTE we settled for Nubiani this night and this place did not disappoint. I definitely have high hopes for COTE after this. The food? 10. Banchan? 10. Vibes? 10. Views? 10. Can’t wait to come back here!

text:
Nubiani is hands-down my favorite Korean BBQ spot in NYC. It’s got everything you’d want—great food, attentive service, and even great lighting for all your food shots. 

This time, we went with the pork set and added a side of marinated short rib. I’d never tried their pork before, so I was really excited. Like most KBBQ places, all the side dishes are free refills, including steamed egg, which is a huge bonus. My personal favorites were the radish and the steamed egg—both so comforting and flavorful.

When the pork arrived, it included pork belly, pork shoulder butt, and pork jowl. The staff grilled everything to perfection, making each bite tender and delicious. We also ordered the japchae as an appetizer, but honestly, the portion was so generous it could’ve been a main course. And let me tell you—it was the best japchae I’ve ever had.

If you’re looking for a KBBQ spot that checks all the boxes, Nubiani is the place to go! 

📍 @Nubiani

• Carrot & Basil — Japanese carrot juice, basil eau de vie & dried tomato liqueur. Savory-forward and honestly such a standout.
• Italian Peach — Campari, crème de pêche, agave & Fever Tree Club. Bitter-sweet and very easy to sip.

What we ate:🥔🍣
• In-house chips
• Tuna nigiri
• Garlic knot pie
• Deviled eggs
• Charcuterie

It’s giving pre-dinner drinks that turn into staying longer than you planned. Hoboken’s bar scene definitely just elevated😉🔑

Ridgewood foodies… I just found one of the BEST Italian spots in North Jersey 🍕🇮🇹
If you’re searching for authentic Italian food in Ridgewood NJ, you NEED to try S. Egidio Pizza Salumi. This might honestly be one of the best Italian restaurants I’ve been to in Bergen County.
We started with the cheese board (so fresh, so flavorful 👌), then ordered the FIAMMA pizza — made with San Marzanos, fior di latte, ’nduja, soppressata piccante, and spicy chile-infused honey… the sweet + spicy combo was unreal. Their pizza is THAT good — perfectly crisp, authentic, and full of flavor.
And the Sorrentina gnocchi? So rich, comforting, and packed with flavor. Every bite tasted homemade and authentic.

text:
Panda Harlem Panda Harlem might just be my favorite spot to eat in Harlem.

It’s an Asian fusion restaurant, but the energy is all Harlem—from the music to the crowd to the vibes.

I keep saying I’m gonna try something new, but that Spicy Kung Pao Chicken hits every single time.

My roommate had the Shanghai Salmon and gave it a solid 10/10.

And the Crab Cakes? All crab, barely any breading—chef’s kiss.

If anyone asks for a place to check out in Harlem, Panda is getting my vote every time.

text: this is rao’s in east harlem nyc. open since 1896. 10 tables. no online booking. no waitlist. no phone number to call. the only way in is to know someone who already has a table. regulars have had the same table on the same night every week for decades and pass their reservations down like family heirlooms. red sauce italian that hasn’t changed in over a century. lemon chicken. meatballs. veal. celebrities politicians and people you’ve definitely seen in a movie have all eaten here. and none of them got a reservation. they knew someone. 128 years. 10 tables. no exceptions. find it on spotworthy. #nyc #nycfood #raos #impossible #italian

text:
📍Lanni’s Cucina one of the area’s best hidden gems ✨

Lanni’s Cucina in Sparkill, NY (20 min from Bergen County) is offering an incredible Italian Omakase experience led by Executive Chef Mike Pekrul, whose culinary journey includes some of NYC’s most prestigious kitchens, including One if by Land, Two if by Sea.

From the warm, intimate ambiance to the thoughtfully curated 13-course tasting menu, every detail felt special. Each course somehow topped the one before, but the Lobster 🦞 Wellington completely stole the show.

If you’re searching for your next date night spot, anniversary dinner, or simply a unique dining experience, add Lanni’s Cucina to your list.

text:
This might be the most “Hong Kong” I've ever felt in NYC🥹They even have hong kong milk tea cocktail, 7-Eleven style fish siu mai and indomie noodle, and a bougie caviar egg tart 😭🇭🇰

@the_collectorsbar, the very first Hong Kong themed speakeasy bar, just opened in Williasmburg🎉 

I was impressed by all the details only Hongkongers would notice—from the foam containers for siu mai to the nostalgic 80s cantopop playlist. 

Even their bartender is from Hong Kong (hi Sean, you’re AMAZING!), so we ended up chatting in Cantonese the whole night and had such a fun time♥️

✎﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏

🍢 𝙎𝙠𝙚𝙬𝙚𝙧𝙨 (𝘾𝙪𝙧𝙧𝙮 𝙁𝙞𝙨𝙝𝙗𝙖𝙡𝙡/𝙁𝙞𝙨𝙝 𝙎𝙝𝙪𝙢𝙖𝙞) $4/5pcs
🍜 𝘿𝙧𝙮 𝙉𝙤𝙤𝙙𝙡𝙚𝙨 $8
Okay I know the prices are diabolical since they're basically HKD converted straight into USD😂 But it's so hard to find these HK street food and 7-Eleven snacks in NYC. They instantly brought back so many school memories, and the dry noodles (aka Indomie) actually paired really well with the cocktails.

🥧 𝘾𝙖𝙫𝙞𝙖𝙧 𝙀𝙜𝙜 𝙏𝙖𝙧𝙩 $10
I had to order this out of curiosity🫣It was the fanciest egg tart I've ever had, topped with crème fraîche and caviar. It paired really well with the HK milk tea cocktail, but I'd probably stick with the classic egg tart ($4) next time.

🌊 𝘿𝙧𝙖𝙜𝙤𝙣 𝙆𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙤𝙛 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙀𝙖𝙨𝙩 𝙎𝙚𝙖 東海龍王 $20
🥃 𝙁𝙡𝙖𝙢𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙈𝙤𝙪𝙣𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙣 火焰山 $22
We ordered two cocktails inspired by Journey to the West/西遊記 (a classic chinese mythological novel). 

🧋 𝙃𝙤𝙣𝙜 𝙆𝙤𝙣𝙜 𝙈𝙞𝙡𝙠 𝙏𝙚𝙖 𝘾𝙤𝙘𝙠𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙡/𝙈𝙤𝙘𝙠𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙡 (𝙤𝙛𝙛 𝙢𝙚𝙣𝙪)
We were told this is the bartender's special for Hongkongers 👀 Made with the classic Black & White evaporated milk (黑白淡奶) and a touch of caramel, the soju base was HK milk tea infused. Hands down our table’s favorite drink of the night.

🍸 𝘽𝙞𝙩𝙩𝙚𝙧 𝙈𝙚𝙡𝙤𝙣 𝙈𝙤𝙘𝙠𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙡, 𝙎𝙩𝙧𝙖𝙬𝙗𝙚𝙧𝙧𝙮 𝙍𝙖𝙢𝙪𝙣𝙚 𝙈𝙤𝙘𝙠𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙡 (𝙤𝙛𝙛 𝙢𝙚𝙣𝙪) 
I don't drink, so the bartender kindly made me two custom mocktails. The bitter melon one totally surprised me and reminded me of a cucumber mocktail, super refreshing, and it was the perfect antidote after eating so much "yit hei" food lol.
